title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Unified Guidelines + ADRs)
author: Samira Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates Redwood Inference architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also records key Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) that shaped the platform runtime and operational choices. This document is intended as the canonical reference for teams building production inference services and operators configuring the platform.

Scope
- Applies to: all teams implementing public or internal HTTP/gRPC APIs, inference serving components, and infra changes that affect SLOs or customer-facing behavior (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Excludes: experimental prototypes kept in personal repos; those should be promoted via a PR and design review to be covered by these standards.

Principles
1. Production-first: every change must preserve or improve documented SLOs and observability.
2. Backwards-compatible by default: API changes should be additive and versioned when incompatible.
3. Measurable: every service must emit metrics, traces, and logs mapped to standard dashboards.
4. Secure by design: follow least privilege for IAM, encrypt data in flight and at rest, and treat customer data as sensitive by default.

1) API standards
- Surface area: primary service names: inference-api, runtime-dispatcher, model-store, kv-cache, batcher.
- Protocols: HTTP/1.1 + TLS 1.2+ for public endpoints; gRPC over TLS for internal service-to-service calls.
- Versioning: use semantic versioned route prefixes for breaking changes: /v1/, /v2/. Non-breaking additions must be omitted via new optional fields.
- Naming: REST resources use kebab-case (e.g., /models/{model-id}/versions).
- Request/response schema: use JSON Schema (openapi v3) for all public endpoints and publish schemas to the API registry.
- Error handling: standard error envelope: {code, message, details[]}. Use HTTP status codes (4xx for client, 5xx for server). Map internal error codes to small, documented machine-readable codes (e.g., INFERENCE_TIMEOUT, MODEL_NOT_FOUND, QUOTA_EXCEEDED).
- Rate limiting & quotas: default rate-limiter is per-API-key with a burst token bucket. Default hosted quotas: 600 req/min API-key; per-route overrides for high-throughput endpoints. For enterprise/Dedicated, quotas configured per-customer in config-service.
- Pagination & streaming: use cursor-based pagination for list endpoints. For generation streaming, use chunked Transfer-Encoding or gRPC server streaming.
- Authentication: JWT-based tokens for hosted; mTLS or signed tokens for private deployments. Keys rotate every 90 days by default (see key-management policy).
- Contract testing: every API must include an OpenAPI contract and a contract test that runs in CI against a mocked service and the integration staging environment.

API Example (excerpt)
POST /v1/generate
Request: {"model": "redwood-13b", "input": "...", "max_tokens": 256}
Response (streaming chunks): {"id":"req-123","chunk_index":0,"text":"Hello"}

2) Coding standards
- Languages: Go (backend services), Python (data & eval pipelines), TypeScript (console/frontend). Exceptions require RFC and owner approval.
- Formatting & linting: gofmt/golangci-lint for Go; Black + ruff for Python; Prettier + ESLint for TypeScript. CI must fail on lint or formatting errors.
- Testing: unit tests target >= 80% function coverage for new modules; integration tests mandatory for API surface area. Use Testcontainers or localstack when appropriate.
- Dependency policy: prefer stable tagged releases; patch-level auto-updates allowed with a weekly review. Major upgrades require an RFC and canary rollout.
- Secrets: do not check secrets into git. Use secrets manager (Vault/KMS) with least privilege.
- Code reviews: at least one approving review from a service owner and one from a cross-team reviewer for infra-impacting changes.

3) Infrastructure standards
- Accounts & networking: services run in named accounts/environments: prod, staging, dev. VPC peering and private link only via infra PR and security review.
- Resource naming: <team>-<service>-<env>-<resource> (e.g., infra-batcher-prod-asg).
- IAM: follow least privilege; use role-based access with short-lived credentials. Owner must document IAM changes in the PR.
- Autoscaling: CPU and custom metrics-driven autoscaling. For inference API frontends, autoscale on p95 latency > target and queue depth.
- Capacity planning: GPU fleet capacity plan updated quarterly. Baseline per-cluster headroom: 20% to accommodate spikes and rolling updates.
- CI/CD: all deployments via the canonical pipeline (ci-cd-and-build). Production deployments require pipeline gating with smoke tests and SLO checkers.

4) Model-serving standards
- Packaging: models stored in model-store with immutable version IDs. A manifest (YAML) must accompany each model with fields: id, architecture, quantization, tokenizer, expected max_seq_len, perf_profile.
- Model variants: all models must declare compatibility tags: [cpu-friendly, gpu-optimized, quantized-8bit, fp16]. Runtime selects variant via policy.
- Quantization & validation: quantized weights require a validation job that checks output deltas against float baseline on a standard eval prompt set (regression threshold < 1.5% task-level delta).
- Warm-starting & KV cache: KV cache TTL default 5 minutes for interactive sessions; explicit cache-control headers can override. Prefix caching allowed for prompt templates but must be opt-in.
- Rollouts: use canary deployments by traffic percentage and compare quality metrics on a holdout prompt set. Abort if quality regression > 2% or error increase > 0.2 percentage points.
- Compatibility matrix: maintain a matrix of runtime-kernel compatibilities per GPU generation in the kernel-and-scheduling directory.

5) Observability standards
- Metrics: follow the standard metric naming prefix: redwood.<service>.<resource>.<metric>. Emit at least: request_count, request_latency_ms (histogram), error_count, model_inference_time_ms, tokens_out.
- Tracing: use OpenTelemetry with 100% sampling in dev/staging and adaptive sampling in prod (default 10% for non-error traces, 100% for error traces). Span naming: <service>.<handler>.<operation>.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, service, env, request_id, user_id (hashed), level, message, tags. Log retention: 90 days by default for infra logs; customer data logs subject to retention policies.
- Dashboards & alerts: every service must publish an SLO dashboard (see SLO library). Alerting thresholds defined in runbooks with on-call rotations and playbook links.
- SLOs: documented in eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets. Examples: 
  - inference-api (hosted): availability (2xx responses) 99.95% monthly; latency p95 < 150ms; error rate < 0.1%
  - inference-api (dedicated): availability 99.9% monthly; latency p95 < 200ms; error rate < 0.2%
- Incident instrumentation: all incidents must include a pre-populated timeline from tracing and a postmortem reference to metrics and dashboards.

6) Performance standards & benchmarking
- Benchmarks: use the canonical benchmarking suite in eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Benchmarks must include: cold-start latency, steady-state throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, and memory usage.
- Target performance (guidelines):
  - Small models (<=7B): p95 generation latency < 80ms for 256 tokens on A100-like hardware; throughput > 800 tokens/sec per GPU.
  - Medium models (7B-15B): p95 < 140ms for 256 tokens; throughput > 400 tokens/sec per GPU.
  - Large models (>15B): p95 < 250ms for 256 tokens; throughput target depends on quantization profile.
- Continuous perf monitoring: perf regressions are tracked by weekly jobs; any regression > 10% in p95 triggers an investigation and may block releases.
- Batching: default batching window 8ms for latency-sensitive routes; larger windows allowed on heavy-throughput routes with documented cost/latency tradeoffs.

7) Decision records (ADRs) - canonical summaries
- ADR 001: Runtime kernel selection (2025-11-12) \u2014 Decision: adopt hybrid kernel selection that prefers precompiled kernels per-model/seq-length profile and falls back to JIT kernels for unsupported shapes. Rationale: reduces p95 latency variance and speeds onboarding of new models. Owner: runtime-team.
- ADR 013: Streaming API format (2026-01-20) \u2014 Decision: use chunked JSON lines for HTTP streaming and gRPC streaming for internal services. Rationale: maximum client compatibility and ease of buf management. Owner: eng-developer-experience.
- ADR 021: Quantization policy (2026-03-05) \u2014 Decision: allow 8-bit quantization for inference with mandatory regression validation and per-customer opt-out. Rationale: significant cost savings with controlled quality risk. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.
- ADR 030: Model variant routing (2026-09-02) \u2014 Decision: introduce policy-driven routing by latency/cost/region with automatic fallback chain {primary_variant, cheaper_compatible_variant, base_float_variant}. Owner: eng-platform.

8) Rollout & change management
- Design review: changes affecting API contract, SLOs, or infra require an ADR or an RFC reviewed by at least two teams: owning team and a cross-cutting reviewer (runtime, infra, or security).
- Canary procedure:
  1) Deploy canary to 1% traffic with enhanced telemetry.
  2) Monitor SLO dashboard and holdout prompt quality for 30 minutes.
  3) If stable, gradually increase to 10% then 50% with automated checks.
  4) Full rollout only after 24h stability on 50% or a documented business exception.
- Rollback criteria: automatic rollback if error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency degrades > 20% relative compared to baseline.

9) Ownership & contact points
- Service owners must be recorded in the service registry and are responsible for maintaining runbooks, dashboards, and post-release validations.
- On-call: follow eng-sre incident process. Primary on-call for inference-api: inference-api-owner-schedule (see oncall-and-incident-response).

10) Compliance & security notes
- Data residency: hosted customer data must remain in the selected region; model-store replication must respect data-residency tags.
- Audit logging: all admin actions (model promote, key rotation, capacity changes) must be recorded in audit-logging with 1-year retention for enterprise customers.
- Pen tests: major infra changes require a security sign-off and a penetration test for private deployments.

Appendix: Example CI check (YAML snippet)
- name: Contract Test
  run: |
    curl -sSf $STAGING_API/health || exit 1
    pytest tests/contract/test_openapi.py --base-url $STAGING_API

Appendix: Sample model manifest (YAML)
- id: redwood-13b-v1
  architecture: transformer-decoder
  tokenizer: bpe-v2
  quantization: q8_0
  max_seq_len: "2048"
  perf_profile: "gpu-a100-256-tokens"
